# Bug Catalog: `game/diver.gd` environmental abilities

**Generated by /design-tests on 2026-08-26**
**Scope:** `Diver`'s three environmental abilities, the real `World` gap puzzle, and the oxygen boundary shared with sonar.

## What this file does

`Diver` owns the public readiness and execution contract for Shockwave,
Grapple, and Swap. `World` routes input into that contract and composes those
abilities into the entrance-blockade, whirlpool, and three-plate progression
puzzle. Combat moves and world spells use separate oxygen paths.

## Public interface

| Symbol | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Diver.can_use_ability()` | query | Reports whether the active environmental ability can start. |
| `Diver.use_ability(aim_dir, target)` | command | Executes Shockwave, Grapple, or Swap through the real gameplay dispatcher. |
| `Diver.toggle_sonar()` | command/query | Toggles the oxygen-consuming sonar boundary that must remain resource-gated. |
| `World` scene | integration surface | Builds the actual blockade, anchors, whirlpool, plates, doors, and goal. |

## Load-bearing comments

- Grapple and Swap misses are documented as costing nothing.
- The highway requires all three divers to cross through Grapple/Swap and
  occupy the three plates simultaneously.
- A save point is currently the only oxygen refill.
- Sonar intentionally remains an oxygen-consuming passive.

## IO boundaries

- Physics: Grapple raycasts against the real far-side `GrappleAnchor`.
- Scene tree: Shockwave broadcasts to `shockwave_breakable`; plates observe
  diver bodies; the goal becomes visible on completion.
- Time: ability cooldowns and Grapple's pull tween.
- Save files: the integration world starts through a throwaway test slot,
  removed after the run.
- Randomness: disabled for the puzzle run so encounters cannot interrupt it.

## Branching points

- ability missing vs. present;
- locked vs. unlocked;
- cooling down or grappling vs. ready;
- zero, partial, or full oxygen;
- Grapple hit vs. miss;
- Swap valid target vs. invalid target;
- all three plates occupied vs. an incomplete set;
- sonar at zero oxygen vs. positive oxygen.

## Magic-string contracts

- `ability_id` is one of `"shockwave"`, `"grapple"`, or `"swap"`, supplied
  by `Diver.BASE_STATS`.
- The real cast order is Mermaid/Swap, Diver Boy/Grapple, Marine
  Man/Shockwave, supplied by `World.CAST` and `Diver.BASE_STATS`.

## Existing tests

`verify/swim.gd` checks movement and animation, while `verify/persistence.gd`
touches Shockwave only to test rock persistence. Neither starts abilities at
zero oxygen or completes the real progression puzzle.

## Bug catalog

| # | Bug (one sentence, failure mode) | Blast radius | Plausibility | Test type | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Zero oxygen disables every environmental ability and permanently strands a puzzle attempt. | High — progression stops after ordinary experimentation. | `can_use_ability()` explicitly compares oxygen against each ability cost. | captured bug + decision table | caught |
| 2 | An environmental ability silently spends combat oxygen, so repeated experimentation creates the same lock later. | High — the player can begin but cannot finish the puzzle. | `use_ability()` deducts before dispatching the ability. | invariant | caught |
| 3 | Removing the oxygen guard only at the input layer leaves the real dispatcher or one ability path blocked. | High — UI appears enabled while an actual ability remains inert. | Readiness and execution are separate methods with three dispatch branches. | differential integration | characterized |
| 4 | A resource fix permits isolated abilities but the real blockade/whirlpool/plate sequence remains unrecoverable. | High — unit tests pass while the shipped puzzle still softlocks. | The puzzle composes repeated Grapples and Swaps with physics and cooldowns. | end-to-end invariant | fixed |
| 5 | A broad “oxygen is free” change accidentally enables sonar at zero oxygen. | Medium — it destroys the remaining overworld oxygen economy. | Sonar shares the same `CombatantStats.oxygen` field but a separate path. | negative path | characterized |
| 6 | Grapple's green preview sees the far anchor but execution hits Diver Boy's own capsule and never pulls. | High — the actual puzzle crossing fails although aiming says it is valid. | Preview excludes the shooter RID; execution did not. | differential integration | fixed |
| 7 | The near staging anchor sits collinear with the far crossing anchor and intercepts every intended crossing shot. | High — the documented traversal sequence cannot begin. | Both valid colliders occupied the same aim line and raycasts select the nearest hit. | end-to-end captured bug | fixed |
| 8 | An ally already across the gap intercepts the next Grapple ray, preventing the repeated crossings needed for all three divers. | High — the sequence fails after one successful crossing. | Rays checked layer 2 even though divers deliberately do not collide with each other. | end-to-end captured bug | fixed |

## Test plan

### Bug #1 — zero-oxygen readiness

- **Test type:** captured bug + bounded decision table
- **Description string:** `environmental oxygen: all three traversal abilities remain ready at zero — guards against puzzle resource lockout`
- **What it catches:** any ability retaining an oxygen threshold.
- **Self-critique:** It asserts the public readiness result across the complete
  three-ability set, not a helper or snapshot. A behavior-preserving refactor
  passes. The bounded input space is exhaustively covered, so a generator adds
  no value.

### Bugs #2 and #3 — execution preserves oxygen and effects

- **Test type:** invariant + differential integration
- **Description string:** `environmental oxygen: zero remains zero while Shockwave, Grapple, and Swap take effect — guards against dispatcher-only fixes and hidden deductions`
- **What it catches:** UI-only fixes, per-ability omissions, and deductions
  before/after execution.
- **Self-critique:** Wrong-but-stable output fails because both world effects
  and exact oxygen preservation are asserted. It does not depend on which
  internal helper implements an ability.

### Bug #4 — real puzzle completion

- **Test type:** end-to-end invariant
- **Description string:** `environmental oxygen: the real gap puzzle completes from an all-zero party — guards against recoverability theater`
- **What it catches:** a locally free ability that still cannot compose into a
  successful shipped puzzle run.
- **Self-critique:** The oracle is the visible goal and all three divers being
  across the hazard, not private call counts or a screenshot.

### Bug #5 — resource boundary

- **Test type:** negative path
- **Description string:** `environmental oxygen: sonar remains unavailable at zero — guards against making the entire oxygen system cosmetic`
- **What it catches:** over-broad removal of oxygen checks.
- **Self-critique:** This directly observes sonar's public toggle result and
  cannot pass if sonar activates incorrectly.

## Skipped

- Combat move oxygen costs — existing battle/balance coverage; a separate
  execution subsystem is unchanged by this fix.
- World-spell oxygen costs — unchanged subsystem; issue #48 is about the three
  environmental abilities.
- Oxygen-bar styling — cosmetic and covered by visual evidence rather than a
  brittle pixel assertion.
- First-time-player comprehension — requires the manual playtest link and an
  unfamiliar player; automation can prove recoverability, not comprehension.

## Post-write evaluation

- **Bugs caught:** #1 and #2 reproduced on current `main`; the real-world test
  then caught #4 and the three traversal blockers recorded as #6–#8.
- **Bugs characterized:** #3 is covered through the public dispatcher and all
  three effect paths; #5 passes because sonar remains unavailable at zero.
- **Bugs discovered during writing:** #6–#8. Grapple preview excluded the
  shooter while execution did not; the near and far anchors were collinear;
  and party members intercepted later crossing rays.
- **Tests removed:** none.

## Notes

The chosen product contract is deliberately global and simple: environmental
abilities are always oxygen-free; sonar, spells, and combat retain their own
resource rules. This avoids puzzle-coordinate exceptions and hidden reserved
oxygen amounts.
